supersedes_or_corrects.correction: OASIS is NOT inference-only / forward-pass-only. The ACL 2026 appendix states that it computes sample-wise gradients, restricted to the last layer; this backward computation adds less than 3.5% overhead relative to a forward pass. It is reference-model-free and substantially cheaper than full gradient-based selection, but describing it as inference-only was incorrect.

new_evidence.result: On Adapt-20, a more dynamic stream with 20 tasks and 19 distribution-shift boundaries, LLaVA-1.5-7B at a 12.5% sample-selection ratio achieved AAUC 55.04±0.89 and Alast 46.84±0.42 with OASIS. Listed alternatives included InfoBatch 54.34±0.68 / 44.59±0.59, DivBS 54.10±0.37 / 43.21±1.02, and GradNorm 52.94±1.11 / 45.02±0.91. This strengthens evidence that online global informativeness + redundancy control retains an advantage when shifts become frequent, not just in short task sequences.
new_evidence.scope: Continual multimodal instruction tuning; 12.5% selection; single benchmark/model configuration for this exact Adapt-20 comparison.

new_evidence.result: OASIS uses Fisher-information-based informativeness from sample-wise last-layer gradients. Appendix A.15 reports the backward computation adds <3.5% overhead relative to the forward pass. Therefore its efficiency claim is low-overhead gradient selection, not inference-only selection.
new_evidence.scope: Implementation detail reported by authors; exact end-to-end selection/training wall-clock depends on model and hardware.

new_evidence.result: In class-incremental CIFAR-100 with a Vision Transformer (20 tasks, 5 new classes every 100 epochs, 2,000 epochs total), ordinary layer norm produced a final-task scratch-vs-incremental gap close to 10 percentage points. Reparameterizing layer norm as (x-normalized)*(1+gamma)+beta reduced that gap to about 4 points before reinitialization methods were applied. With reparameterized layer norm, selective weight reinitialization was the only compared reinitialization method that maintained stable performance across all 20 runs; ReDo and continual backprop suffered last-task learning instabilities. Selective weight reinitialization still fell below the from-scratch reference on the final tasks, so it only partially solved plasticity loss.
new_evidence.scope: Continual supervised class-incremental CIFAR-100 with ViT; old classes remained in training data specifically to isolate plasticity from forgetting. This is evidence about plasticity, not a catastrophic-forgetting solution.

new_evidence.result: The authors explicitly state they did not study forgetting and there is no evidence the reinitialization algorithms prevent it; because reinitialization erases parameters, it may exacerbate forgetting unless utility is computed using past/current observations or combined with rehearsal.
new_evidence.scope: Important negative boundary: do not promote selective weight reinitialization as a standalone anti-forgetting mechanism.

candidate_updates.update: Strengthened: Adapt-20 shows OASIS advantage with 19 shifts at 12.5% selection. Correct mechanism description to low-overhead last-layer-gradient/Fisher online selection plus redundancy reduction, not inference-only selection.
candidate_updates.confidence: high on online selection principle in continual instruction tuning; medium on transfer outside supervised/instruction streams

candidate_updates.update: Refined: selective weight reinitialization is robust to small networks and layer norm and is the most stable compared reinitialization scheme in the reported ViT/CIFAR-100 setup, but it addresses plasticity rather than forgetting. Reparameterized layer norm itself is a large part of the gain (roughly reducing final-task scratch gap from ~10 to ~4 points), so parameter renewal should be evaluated jointly with gradient-flow-preserving normalization.
candidate_updates.confidence: high on plasticity result; low-to-medium as standalone continual-memory mechanism

negative_and_boundary_evidence.claim: Gradient-based online selection need not be prohibitively expensive.
negative_and_boundary_evidence.scope: OASIS reports <3.5% backward overhead relative to forward when restricting gradients to the last layer; not a universal hardware-independent overhead bound.

negative_and_boundary_evidence.claim: Plasticity preservation and forgetting prevention are separate objectives.
negative_and_boundary_evidence.scope: The selective-weight-reinitialization ViT experiment deliberately retains old-class training data and explicitly disclaims evidence for forgetting prevention.

negative_and_boundary_evidence.claim: Normalization dynamics can themselves create apparent continual-learning failure.
negative_and_boundary_evidence.scope: In this ViT/CIFAR-100 setup, the layer-norm scale collapsed and shrank gradients; reparameterized layer norm substantially narrowed the plasticity gap. Generalization to other architectures requires testing.

rejected_or_deprioritized_leads.lead: Treat selective weight reinitialization as a unified solution for retention
rejected_or_deprioritized_leads.reason: Rejected. Primary paper explicitly separates plasticity from forgetting and warns reinitialization may worsen forgetting. Keep it only as a plasticity-maintenance component that likely needs rehearsal/retention constraints.
Rejected as factually incorrect after appendix inspection; it computes last-layer sample-wise gradients.
